headline: Multi-omic and long-read models resolve regulatory and mutational state in cancer genomes
label: Cancer Multi Omic Regulatory Modeling
summary: New cancer genomics work couples multi-omic integration with long-read and perturbation data to attribute regulatory and mutational state more precisely.
synthesis: The dominant thread is extracting finer-grained regulatory and mutational information from cancer multi-omic data. FiberTron predicts base-resolution methylation and accessibility from a single Fiber-seq/Nanopore sample, while a Perturb-seq CRISPRi framework with ENCODE TF binding priors infers TNBC regulatory networks and is reported to outperform GENIE3 and co-expression. Survival modelling is the second strand: a benchmark of joint dimension reduction finds JIVE and RGCCA strongest, and UniPanSurv and Pathway-Transformer add pan-cancer zero- and few-shot transfer and transcript-variant pathway features. Mutational-process work (refined InDel taxonomy, SEQUENCE) addresses signature bias. Long-read somatic calling and sample-mispairing benchmarks address upstream data quality. Explicit cell-type attribution is largely absent from these items.
